wsl-claude: yes, three things outside the interface's consumers, one of them serious. Checked in the tree:
1) SERIOUS: THE REPLAY PROTECTION'S BACKUP. node.db holds the replay index (it stops a replayed message from being acted on twice), and it's designed as REBUILDABLE FROM THE LOG: nodeStore.js:329, 'every hash here is also in traffic.jsonl. Losing node.db costs a rebuild, not the protection: a derived thing that cannot be rebuilt is a single point of silent weakening.' Put the log INSIDE node.db, and losing node.db loses the log AND the index's backup together. So either the log goes into its OWN database file (log.db), or that promise is given up knowingly. I'd say log.db.
2) SPEED OF EVERY POST: node.db writes with synchronous = FULL and journal_mode = DELETE (nodeStore.js:192-193): every write waits for the disk, and a writer blocks readers. Today each post already writes the replay row there; adding the log row doubles that on the path of every message. A separate log.db avoids that too.
3) THREE TESTS read traffic.jsonl directly (liveFrontDoor.js:88, measureCapacity.js:322, queueRestart.js:52). Tests may, by your rule, but they'd break at the switch; that's mine to move to the interface first.
And one human thing: the .jsonl is a file you can open and read. The database isn't. If that matters, an export.

Your call, recorded: the log goes into node.db, and backups carry the risk. One fact so the rule is honest: SpiritOS has no backup of relay-state today; nothing in the tree makes one. What exists is that node.db is safe to copy as a file once a write has finished (nodeStore.js:44-46, rollback journal). So 'rely on backups' means your own copy of relay-state, from outside the node. Also, nodeStore.js:329's promise that 'losing node.db costs a rebuild' stops being true, and gets rewritten citing your words, not left to mislead. Shall R19.1 go on the board as: 'The log moves into a table in node.db behind its existing api; losing node.db is covered by the owner's backups, not by a rebuild'?

wsl-claude: your call, and taken. Two facts so it's decided knowingly, then I'll drop it:
1) That rebuild promise is a written condition of cycle 10 (design/cycles/2026-09-23-sealed-posts-cycle-10.md:1315-1318, 'the index rebuilds from the log... a derived thing that cannot be rebuilt is a single point of silent weakening'). Accepting the risk retires that condition, so the move should say so in that cycle doc, not leave it silently untrue.
2) 'Rely on backups': there is no backup of relay-state/ or node.db anywhere in the tree today (nothing in bash/ or the node). So if backups are the safety, one has to exist.
The SPEED point (every post waits for the disk twice in node.db) isn't about risk, though. A separate file still helps there, whatever you decide about the rebuild.
